scopeNote: This assessment expands the previous product-only scope to include secure, reliable production operation. The lower total reflects the wider goal, not a measured regression in reverse-engineering features.
assessmentNote: Quality run [40242498764](https://github.com/xdCloudy/REAmon/actions/runs/40242498764) passed on commit `398d32ae`. The OCI label and live readiness payload both matched that tested SHA with a clean source state. All five jobs passed: webapp checks, the canonical Docker unit gate, agent dependency audit, Compose validation, and production image smoke. The live-stack smoke included authenticated acceptance, browser login, two-replica worker crash/recovery, bounded load and soak, PostgreSQL/artifact restore, and Neo4j dump/restore. This resolves the earlier pending fixed-source CI and login/unit-gate claims; it does not establish the state of the user's LAN deployment or close source-level security findings. Four of five validated security findings have source mitigations; shared Kali shell and `/tmp` cross-user access remains open. The legacy unscoped agent file-download route has now been removed; the shell-level finding remains unresolved. Other release work includes independent review and LAN verification of storage admission and service controls, per-user isolation before restoring user-configured MCP stdio, and broader source/deployment review. Weighted progress remains an evidence-based estimate, not release certification.

workstreams.name: Core analysis and visualizer workflow
workstreams.summary: Imports, provider execution, database-backed code units, source navigation, and a multi-provider visualizer are established across several language and binary workflows. A worker-run SLB2 inspection of the 1.26 GB PS5 QA artifact completed and persisted two bounded container facts; wider fixture validation remains open.
workstreams.remaining: Provider runtime and fidelity vary by format. Broad real-world fixture comparison, remaining provider validation, and consistent recovery across large projects are still open.
workstreams.basis: Imports, provider execution, stored code units, source navigation, and review workflows exist. The profiler recognizes structurally plausible PyInstaller CArchive cookies in native executables and records package/runtime metadata. A pinned, MIT-licensed pyinstxtractor-go snapshot now runs in a bounded isolated service, extracts capped Python bytecode children, persists each accepted child as a task-scoped derived artifact and database code unit, and feeds up to four not-yet-decompiled modules per run to pycdc while skipping exact-hash modules already completed in prior project runs; child records retain executable, archive-path, extractor-revision, bytecode-hash, and recovered-source provenance. The Go image builds and webapp type-checks; representative archive execution and fidelity validation remain open. The Python bytecode workflow pairs hash-verified recovered source with bounded bytecode in the visualizer and MCP dossier, keeps module-wide evidence out of selected-function context, and carries the raw bytecode magic without inferring a runtime version. Native Mach-O analysis stores exact-address Swift/Objective-C metadata and exposes capped, hash-checked ReIPA pseudocode alternatives; the visualizer can compare native provider outputs by canonical function identity across differing saved paths and output-language labels. Isolated pinned Glaurung, Kuna, and Fission providers persist bounded native C-like pseudocode; Fission's exact-hash per-function outputs are included as same-function AI context only after binary-hash, identity, completed-run, and output-hash checks. Kuna also stores assembly, selected call/jump/reference edges, and bounded opcode sequences. A pinned isolated Recurse MCP adapter stores bounded per-function VTIL-style lift evidence and optimizer counters, displayed with its semantic limits; container build, runtime, and fixture comparison remain open. The visualizer and rewrite context compare Ghidra/Kuna instruction sequences across providers only when normalized architecture groups agree, exclude same-function cross-provider self-matches, and keep provider, analysis-run, artifact-hash, identity, and similarity provenance with reused names. Kuna's v1.878 analyzer image and end-to-end worker have been exercised against a system ELF binary. A read-only Ghidra p-code emulator also persists bounded, confidence-labeled control-flow-flattening transitions as visualizer navigation evidence. Ghidra now offers separate opt-in pinned BcfClean and CffDeflatten passes with bounded scans, emulation audits, and hash-checked alternatives in the visualizer and rewrite context; runtime and representative fixture comparisons remain open. The new Fission adapter still needs image-build, runtime, and fixture comparison. Newly settled decompile/disassemble tasks now persist a centralized coverage inventory after database ingestion, separating provider-discovered, provider-returned, raw-observed, and indexed units, along with the unreturned remainder, not-observed and not-indexed counts, explicit WebAssembly invalid/excess record omissions, unvisited functions when discovered and visited counts exist, truncation, and classifications the provider reported. The visualizer uses the stored inventory, shows not-visited units only when discovered and visited counts exist, and labels older runs without it. TypeScript type-check and targeted ESLint pass; provider coverage and runtime behavior remain to be exercised, and unsupported/skip/exclusion classifications remain unknown when engines do not report them. The pinned univdreams analyzer stores a bounded `.ud` module view, compile-back binary, exact hashes, provider revision, and byte-identity result; the selected-unit visualizer reports that result with its limits. A generated 34-byte WASM module, a small synthetic static ELF, an optimized dynamic ELF, and a debug dynamic ELF completed the isolated runtime smoke with byte-identical compile-back. A narrow REAmon-owned univdreams backport clamps non-PLT ranges at named PLT boundaries; maintained-source validation also compiled and persisted the debug ELF with a verified output hash. These synthetic cases do not establish broad format coverage or behavioral fidelity. A separate pinned Miasm provider now lifts executable-section symbol/entry-point candidates in PE/ELF to bounded simplified IR, stores hash-attributed per-function artifacts and block-count changes, and makes exact same-function evidence available to rewrite and MCP context only after identity, run, input-hash, and output-hash checks; x86-64 and AArch64 ELF plus two-function synthetic PE DLL export API smokes pass; other architectures and fixture comparisons remain open. The worker registry now receives an independent 30-second process heartbeat during synchronous analyzer runs, and graph projection is queued outside the analysis polling loop; runtime validation of this revision remains pending. A bounded SLB2 inspector is wired to stored artifact profiles; the real QA PUP table shape and 1.26 GB declared size match the stored artifact, and production build and provider registration passed; a worker-run task against the real 1.26 GB QA PUP completed and persisted two accepted facts plus analysis evidence without decryption. Broader firmware and language fixtures remain open.

workstreams.name: Database-grounded project memory and provenance
workstreams.summary: Project observations, symbols, relationships, source drafts, review receipts, hashes, provider versions, and run evidence ground AI context and cross-provider name reuse. Analyst-reviewed cross-artifact function matches now persist exact pair evidence and supply bounded naming context to explanations and rewrites for exact matched functions, with duplicate pair records resolved by their latest analyst review. Their matcher includes a separately stored, low-weight exact string-reference overlap when both providers supply complete lists. A bounded REA Evidence v2 bundle importer validates canonical identities and manifests, stores complete provider-attributed records idempotently, links only exact artifact hashes, and supplies a bounded untrusted subset to rewrite context.
workstreams.remaining: Coverage and consistency still need validation across all formats, providers, and long-running project histories.
workstreams.basis: Project-scoped observations, symbols, relationships, drafts, and review records ground AI context. Common native virtual-address spellings now canonicalize across Ghidra, Glaurung, and Oxidizer for same-artifact function identity; bounded same-binary, completed-run lookups bring accepted cross-provider names into rewrite, explanation, and MCP dossier contexts for selected units with canonical-key or normalized native-identity matches, exact input-hash checks, and review-receipt verification. Durable function-pair records now preserve exact artifact hashes, analysis tasks, provider versions, function identities, bounded instruction/CFG snapshots, and append-only reviews; accepted pair names enter explanation context only when both the selected function identity and artifact hash match, with score and review provenance, and never auto-rename maintained source. Ghidra/Kuna lookalike context now retains the producing provider, analysis task, artifact identity and hash, normalized architecture, native function identity, and similarity score; opening an older match resolves its exact completed run only within the active project artifact selection. Fission, Ghidra, and Kuna same-function native reconstructions can now enter selected-unit rewrite context only when the input artifact hash, canonical address identity, completed provider run, and saved output hash all match; each is labeled provisional provider evidence. Recurse VTIL-style lift artifacts persist exact input/output hashes, provider revision, native function identity, and optimizer counters; rewrite context reads a same-function lift only from a completed run with exact input, identity, run-path, and output-hash checks, while labeling the lift as provisional structural evidence. Legacy native address aliases remain a fallback and are labeled separately because they can denote thunks. MCP provider outputs also require exact input and saved-output hashes; accepted project-memory lookup is bounded to 100 candidate provider observations and reports possible truncation. Exact-address ReIPA pseudocode alternatives for matched Swift/Objective-C methods enter rewrite context and MCP dossiers only after same-run provenance checks. Ghidra functions persist bounded basic-block/edge/entry/exit metrics and a bounded basic-block graph for the visualizer. Control-flow-flattening recovery now persists in function observation attributes and is available to the visualizer, rewrite/explanation, and MCP dossier as confidence-labeled structural evidence; it does not establish identity or behavior. Opt-in BcfClean and CffDeflatten pseudocode enters rewrite context only after the pinned provider version, same-artifact hash, exact address, saved-output hash, and successful emulation audit all match. The MCP code dossier now recomputes maintained-source and saved-draft hashes before exposing their code or validator results; Python bytecode units now retain hashes for both reconstructed source and disassembly, and the visualizer, MCP dossier, and module-level rewrite context verify those hashes; module-wide bytecode evidence is withheld from selected-function context unless a unique same-module code-object name match exists; maintained code also requires an accepted receipt matching the exact source bytes. Rewrite context now reads accepted symbols from immutable receipt snapshots and rehashes maintained callee source before using it. The visualizer and Ghidra export use the accepted receipt’s same symbol snapshot for historical rename names, lineage, and address annotations. Broader identity coverage and fixture validation remain open. PyInstaller bytecode children now persist as task-scoped derived artifacts with database code-unit records linking each module to the executable hash, archive member, extractor revision, and bytecode hash; up to four selected modules gain hash-verified pycdc source provenance, while remaining modules retain bytecode evidence for later review. PyInstaller selection now queries prior project observations using the exact executable hash and stable module code-unit key, so repeated runs continue through pending modules instead of restarting the same four-module batch. Scope-safe rename proposals are persisted as proposal-only attempts with the exact editable source and hash, accepted project-symbol context and hash, provider/model, and mappings; applied attempts link to that proposal and verify selected mappings against it. Attempt history displays and reloads saved proposals only after the current source hash and provider match. Prior proposals enter later AI prompts as unreviewed hints, never accepted evidence. TypeScript type-check, targeted ESLint, and Python AST parsing pass; runtime workflow and fixture evidence remain pending. The univdreams module observation stores the source and compile-back artifact paths, exact input/source/output hashes, pinned provider revision, and byte-identity verdict in the project database; the visualizer reads the persisted verdict rather than inferring it. Maintained Universal Dreams source validation now stores the compiler output as a source-and-output-hash-addressed artifact under the exact analysis run; the immutable review record carries that artifact path, output hash, source hash, and pinned compiler method. A maintained debug-ELF .ud module compiled back byte-identically after the narrow PLT-overlap backport, and the persisted artifact hash was independently checked; other format and behavior fixtures remain open. The REA Evidence v2 importer caps uploads at 8 MiB and 1,000 records, validates strict record shapes, profile and semantic hashes, record order and derived bundle manifests, then stores complete records with project-scoped idempotency. Only one exact project artifact SHA-256 match creates a link; unmatched or ambiguous records stay unbound. Up to twelve records for that exact artifact enter rewrite context as external untrusted data with their provider, confidence, authority, and limitations. Residual-unknown revision histories are explicitly unsupported and rejected rather than dropped; a searchable evidence review and explanation/MCP retrieval remain open.

workstreams.name: Major-language and format decompilation fluency
workstreams.summary: Useful Java, Android, .NET, Python, WebAssembly, native, and additional format paths exist at different maturity levels.
workstreams.remaining: Major languages need idiomatic source recovery, broader project-level coverage, and versioned validation; several formats remain alternate views or early experiments.
workstreams.basis: Several useful Java, .NET, Android, Python, WebAssembly, and native paths exist, and matched arm64 Mach-O methods can now show early ReIPA C-like pseudocode beside Ghidra output; optional Glaurung and Kuna providers add bounded native C-like pseudocode, with Kuna also saving assembly and selected graph edges. Kuna's analyzer has built and completed an end-to-end system-ELF smoke run. Reko 0.12.5 now also passes an isolated runtime smoke on a generated PE, returning two address-keyed function artifacts with exact hashes. These native alternates still need representative fixture comparison and fidelity validation. Many languages remain navigation-only, early, or represented by generic pseudocode. The new isolated Arlecchino provider builds from its audited upstream revision, combines Vineflower, CFR, and JADX per class using compiler-error ranking, and stores canonical rename provenance, round-trip coverage, and hash-attributed output. Runtime and fixture fidelity remain unverified, so this adds a limited early JVM capability only. The pycdc provider stores a hash-attributed recovered Python source artifact and bounded bytecode disassembly, both linked to Python source units and verified by the visualizer. Selected-function context can include an exact-run code-object section when one matching name exists in the module, while ambiguous matches are omitted; module context retains the bounded full listing. A bounded isolated PyInstaller extractor now sends recovered `.pyc` members through that provider and preserves executable, archive-member, bytecode, and source hashes; only image-build and type-check evidence exist so far, so execution and source fidelity remain unvalidated. The ILSpy provider now applies a pinned NoFuserEx static ConfuserEx cleanup subset before decompilation, stores transformed assemblies separately with exact input/output hashes and pass provenance, and labels the output as intermediate; the image builds, while fixture-backed fidelity remains open. The webcrack analyzer also recovers embedded JavaScript/TypeScript from bounded local version 3 source maps, storing exact map and content provenance; maps are optional build evidence and may be stale, so broad TypeScript bundle reconstruction remains open. The isolated ILSpy analyzer now emits bounded, syntax-parsed Visual Basic-shaped translations from its C# reconstruction with exact source/output hashes and pinned CodeConverter provenance; this is an early bridge only, not recovered original VB, and fixture compilation and behavior checks remain open. A constrained CRuby 3.4.11 provider recognizes YARB ISeq artifacts and stores bounded raw disassembly plus a hash-verified structured sequence/opcode tree with locals, parameters, catch entries, opcode operands, and an early label-derived CFG. A bounded BSD-2-Clause Ruby 2.7-focused adapter now creates an experimental source candidate as a separate artifact when it passes CRuby 3.4.11 syntax parsing; the upstream is version-mismatched, so syntax acceptance does not establish behavior or fidelity. Vineflower now integrates the pinned Apache-2.0 Java Deobfuscator static Allatori flow pass for bounded JARs and stores a separate transformed artifact plus alternate sources when supported patterns are found; target code is not run, and behavior/fidelity comparison remains open. The pinned analyzer image now builds with the Allatori pass; provider runtime and fixture-backed fidelity remain open. A pinned isolated univdreams provider adds a low-level editable `.ud` view and compile-back evidence for supported ELF, PE, NE, thin Mach-O, WASM, and 6502 raw inputs. REAmon now byte-identically round-trips a minimal WASM module, small synthetic static ELF, optimized dynamic ELF, and debug dynamic ELF after a narrow PLT-overlap backport; maintained debug-ELF source validation also compiled and persisted the hash-verified binary. These small synthetic cases do not establish broad format coverage, behavior, or idiomatic source recovery. The pinned GPL-2.0-only Miasm adapter adds a provisional native deobfuscation view for supported PE/ELF architectures; x86-64 and AArch64 ELF plus two-function synthetic PE DLL export API smokes pass; broader architecture and fixture-backed fidelity remain open, and it does not produce original-language source.

workstreams.name: Maintainable editing, review, and export
workstreams.summary: Hash-bound drafts and immutable review receipts preserve lineage, with syntax validation, an early Java rebuild, and language-specific rename workflows now extending to C/C++ local bindings.
workstreams.remaining: Project-wide edits, cross-file builds, more target-format rebuilds, and runtime or behavior validation remain limited; representative C/C++ projects and compiler-version coverage still need evaluation.
workstreams.basis: Hash-bound drafts and review receipts preserve exact source lineage. New accepted reviews snapshot the exact source and symbol index; the visualizer can restore a verified prior source into a new review using that revision's saved rename context. Accepted-source promotion rejects failed or unavailable validation and prevents a previously accepted language-specific syntax check from silently downgrading to generic Tree-sitter evidence. An initial JVM rebuild path compiles one receipt-verified accepted Java class against the original JAR in the isolated JDK analyzer, patches matching class entries into a separate unsigned derived JAR, removes stale nested class files, and records the input/source/output hashes and compiler version in project observations. This is single-class build evidence only: signed and multi-release JARs, external dependency classpaths, cross-file builds, and runtime/fixture validation remain open. Syntax-aware edits cover selected languages, with reproducible export; the visualizer now exposes hash-pinned Phpactor LSP local-variable and parameter renames for PHP, validates rewritten source with PHP lint, and records the rename engine, mappings, and hashes in the existing reviewable attempt flow. A new C/C++ clangd adapter identifies same-file local variables and parameters, rejects unsupported macro/conditional/template forms and existing identifier collisions, checks edits against clangd's exact reference set, and stores the resulting mappings and hashes through the same attempt flow. The agent image builds and seven targeted synthetic C/C++ integration checks pass for grammar loading, local and parameter discovery, hash-bound semantic edits, stale-source and collision rejection, macro/template exclusions, and GCC/G++ syntax-check acceptance and rejection. Representative projects, complete reference coverage, and behavioral equivalence remain unvalidated. Broad language coverage and project-level edits remain limited. Saved rename proposals can be reviewed after reload and restored into the editor only when their source hash and provider still match; applying them remains a separate reviewed action. The proposal stage is explicitly marked unvalidated, and the resulting scope-aware transformation keeps its syntax/binding validation record and proposal lineage. Type-check and targeted lint pass; runtime rename fixtures remain open. Universal Dreams `.ud` edits now pass the pinned verify-and-compile step before acceptance, with compiled bytes stored under run evidence and the exact source/output hashes and path written into the immutable review receipt. The isolated container build, webapp type-check, and one synthetic WASM runtime validation pass; format and behavior fixture coverage remain open.

workstreams.name: Fixture-backed validation and fidelity evidence
workstreams.summary: Provider smoke checks, structural validators, and a small number of synthetic round-trip cases provide early evidence.
workstreams.remaining: Build a broad, versioned fixture suite for clean, optimized, stripped, and obfuscated inputs and compare recovered behavior and fidelity.
workstreams.basis: Provider smoke checks and structural validators exist, but broad versioned clean, optimized, stripped, and obfuscated fixture comparisons are still missing.

workstreams.name: Security, reliability, and production operations
workstreams.summary: Four of five findings validated in the repository-wide source review have source mitigations. User-configured stdio MCP execution remains disabled at webapp and agent boundaries pending isolation; global tunnel credential access is restricted to the master key and returns a sanitized origin; shared artifact-volume exhaustion has dynamic free-space admission and active-import reservations; MCP deletion responses mask retained credential values. Shared Kali shell and `/tmp` cross-user disclosure remains open. Quality run [40242498764](https://github.com/xdCloudy/REAmon/actions/runs/40242498764) passed all five CI jobs, including the complete canonical Docker unit gate and production-stack acceptance, browser login, worker recovery/load, and PostgreSQL/artifact plus Neo4j backup/restore drills. Independent source review and validation against the user's LAN deployment remain incomplete. The legacy agent `/files?path=/tmp/...` endpoint is removed; project-authorized workspace downloads remain. Its focused Docker regression passes (2 tests), but shared Kali shell and `/tmp` access remain open. The ticket-authenticated Kali terminal proxy now forwards user, project, and session identity before shell startup and discards browser-supplied identity frames; its focused Docker tests pass. This closes identity spoofing at terminal setup, not the shared-shell filesystem exposure.
workstreams.remaining: Remediate cross-user Kali temporary-file disclosure; independently review storage admission; validate service rebuilds and controls on the LAN deployment; implement per-user process isolation before restoring user-configured MCP stdio; and complete broader security, upgrade, backup, and restore review on the deployed release candidate.
workstreams.basis: The estimate rises from 56% to 61% because the fixed source now passes the complete canonical unit gate and production-stack acceptance, including login, worker recovery/load, and database/artifact restore drills in quality run 40242498764. Four of five validated findings have source mitigations. The Kali temporary-file disclosure, independent capacity review, and LAN deployment validation remain open; CI success is not release certification. Removing the obsolete unscoped temporary-file download endpoint and passing its focused Docker regression closes a direct read path, but does not resolve shared shell access or satisfy project-scoped worker isolation; the estimate remains 61%. Ticket-derived terminal identity now takes precedence over browser init data, verified by three focused Docker tests. This is a partial boundary correction; the shared container, workspace mount, and temporary directory remain exposed, so the estimate remains 61%.
